## SEO Keyword Intent Clusterer
**CSV in, content-plan-ready spreadsheet out.**

1. Attach your Telegram credential to every Telegram node.
2. Create an **HTTP Header Auth** credential named `OpenRouter API Key` (header `Authorization`, value `Bearer sk-or-...`) and attach it to both OpenRouter nodes.
3. Tune `batchSize` and `maxKeywords` in the **Config** node.
4. Activate, then send the bot `/help`.

### Two-pass clustering

Pass one classifies keywords in batches, which is fast but lets each batch invent its own cluster names.

Pass two takes only the distinct labels and merges near duplicates into a canonical set with a pillar page title each.

If pass two fails, the raw labels survive and the workflow still delivers.

### Failure behaviour

Batches are matched back to keywords **by keyword string, not item index**, so a failed batch cannot shift every downstream row.

Failed keywords come through marked `unclassified`, the user is told how many batches dropped, and the spreadsheet is still delivered.

parameters.text: SEO Keyword Intent Clusterer Upload a CSV or TXT of raw keywords and you get back a spreadsheet that is ready for content planning: search intent, funnel stage, topic cluster, recommended page format and priority for every keyword. File format One keyword per row. A header row is detected automatically, and a column named keyword, query or term will be used if present. Comma, semicolon, tab and pipe delimiters all work. Optional columns Any volume, difficulty or cpc column is carried straight through into the output, so your existing metrics sit next to the intent data. Output An .xlsx grouped by cluster with the highest value clusters first, plus a short summary message with the intent mix and where to start. Just send the file to begin.
Send me a CSV or TXT file of keywords, one per row, and I will classify and cluster them. Send /help for the full format guide.

This is usually a rate limit or a model timeout, so a retry with a smaller batchSize in the Config node normally clears it.
